items.body:
Simplicity Cremations has opened its first UK store, providing a welcoming space where locals can speak with a funeral specialist, discuss funeral wishes, ask questions and explore planning options.
Located in Long Eaton, the store will bring a shop unit back into use on the high street and reflects wider calls, including recent comments by Andy Burnham, to revitalise town centres and restore local pride.
The modernised store offers a contemporary high-street alternative to the traditional funeral home and will offer information about Simplicity Cremations’ funeral plans, including its latest offering, the Simple Celebration plan.
Building on direct cremation, the new plan gives families the option of a 20-minute, family-led farewell with the coffin present where up to 25 guests can gather for music, readings and tributes.
The store responds to growing interest in simpler funerals, with direct cremation and the new Simple Celebration plan available. Simplicity’s approach removes traditional elements such as flowers, hearses and limousines, focusing instead on meaningful farewells and dignified local care.
Simplicity Cremations is part of the Life Services Group, which has a network of 545 funeral directors, 200 care centres and 45 crematoria that help families access care close to home and choose where their loved one is cremated.
For Long Eaton families, that includes Trent Valley Crematorium, which gives locals the opportunity to keep their final arrangements close to the community they call home.
Colin Wallace, cluster manager for Simplicity Cremations, said: “We’re delighted to have opened our first Simplicity Cremations store in Long Eaton, bringing a fresh new look to the high street. We want local people to have somewhere friendly to come in, speak face to face and get clear answers about funeral planning and that’s exactly what this new space will do.
“We know it can mean a lot to families to have a local crematorium, in a community they know and feel connected to and that’s why customers choosing Simplicity Cremations can also benefit from our vast network, which includes Trent Valley Crematorium, giving them the option to keep arrangements close to home.”
The store is open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm and locals are invited to drop in, meet the team, enjoy a free tea or coffee and have an informal chat about their future wishes and funeral plans.
As part of the Life Services Group, Simplicity Cremations has access to one of the UK’s largest crematorium networks, so it can oversee every part of the process and provide care close to home

items.title: Southern Co-op donates £10,500 to Retail Trust
items.summary: Southern Co-op has donated £10,500 to retail industry charity the Retail Trust, helping to provide vital support to frontline retail workers across the UK. The donation follows Southern Co-op’s Pop in and Win summer activity, which gave customers the chance to win their shopping for… This story continues at Southern Co-op donates £10,500 to Retail Trust Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The donation follows Southern Co-op’s Pop in and Win summer activity, which gave customers the chance to win their shopping for free, with £1 pledged to the Retail Trust for every free shop awarded.
The £10,500 donation will be used to help fund the charity’s Let’s Respect Retail campaign, which provides specialist training, emotional support and access to counselling to help colleagues respond to and recover from abusive incidents.
The Retail Trust will also be encouraging shoppers to show kindness and respect towards retail workers in the run up to Christmas by highlighting how small gestures, such a greeting, a thank you or a smile, can make a real difference during one of their busiest periods of the year. Hundreds of other businesses will also back the Retail Trust’s Let’s Respect Retail campaign by joining the charity in calling for more respect for staff and increasing support for employees.
Rebecca Longyear, community lead at Southern Co-op, said: “We’re really pleased that our summer campaign has not only helped thousands of customers, but has also raised money for such an important cause.
“Our colleagues work incredibly hard to support their communities every day, and everyone deserves to feel safe and respected at work. We’re so proud to support the Retail Trust and the important work it does to make a difference to retail workers across the country.”
Chris Brook-Carter, chief executive of the Retail Trust, said: “This generous donation from Southern Co-op and its customers will allow us to provide even more help to retail workers at risk of abuse as Christmas gets closer and shoppers come under more pressure.
“We’ll be training staff, providing support to those affected and encouraging everyone to show more respect towards the people working hard to serve us. Even something as simple as a greeting or a smile can go a long way, especially for someone facing daily disrespect and hostility.”

items.body:
AllSaints (“the Group”), the global contemporary fashion brand, today announces the appointment of Emine Kaptanoglu as global digital director, who joined the business on 2 November 2026.
Emine brings over 15 years’ experience in premium digital and retail, with a proven track record of building and leading successful teams as well as driving profitable e-commerce growth and digital transformation. She joins AllSaints from Reiss, where she spent more than seven years, most recently as head of e-commerce & customer, managing the global e-commerce strategy and leading the end-to-end platform transformation, driving significant year-on-year digital revenue growth. Prior to that, she also worked at Topshop, as senior digital trading manager.
In her role as global digital director, Emine will have global responsibility for the digital commercial strategy and online customer experience of AllSaints and John Varvatos, bringing her expertise to both brands across all regions and channels. She will report to chief executive officer of the Group, Peter Wood.
Emine’s appointment further strengthens the senior leadership team, following several changes over the past year. Sean Trend joined as chief financial officer in February 2026 and Nichole Strydom as chief merchant in May 2026, while Aaron Esh, who joined as chief creative officer in November 2025, has led the implementation of a refreshed brand identity announced in September 2026.
Peter Wood, chief executive officer of AllSaints, said: “Emine has a proven track record of bringing teams together and delivering great results, with creative energy and a forward-looking vision. We are thrilled to welcome her to our senior leadership team. Her expertise in digital and premium retail, and her success in driving profitable e-commerce growth, will be invaluable as we continue to accelerate our global digital expansion.”
Emine Kaptanoglu, global digital director of AllSaints, said: “AllSaints and John Varvatos are brands with a distinctive identity and a loyal global following. I’m delighted to join at such an exciting time for the Group and to work with colleagues across the organisation to deliver an exceptional digital experience for customers and support the continued evolution of both brands.”

items.title: Retailers need to understand if a cyberattack on one freezer can cause wider disruption, says expert

Following the cyberattacks on supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe, Dai Vaughan, chief technology officer at digital transformation consultancy Public Digital and co-founder of the UK Government Digital Service (GDS) says businesses need safeguards in place to limit damage. “Cyberattacks don’t have to bring down computer systems to cause serious damage. As these supermarket attacks […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following the cyberattacks on supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe, Dai Vaughan, chief technology officer at digital transformation consultancy Public Digital and co-founder of the UK Government Digital Service (GDS) says businesses need safeguards in place to limit damage.
“Cyberattacks don’t have to bring down computer systems to cause serious damage. As these supermarket attacks show, something as simple as changing the temperature of a freezer can destroy thousands of pounds worth of stock.
“More and more of the equipment we rely on is now connected to the internet, from supermarket fridges to heating systems and factory machinery. That makes it easier to manage, but it also creates new risks if security isn’t properly considered and maintained. The security of these systems has to keep pace with how much we rely on them.
“Businesses may have outsourced the maintenance of their equipment, but they haven’t outsourced responsibility for what happens when it fails. They need to know who can access these systems remotely, how that access is protected and whether an attacker could use it to cause wider disruption.
“Cyberattacks are a question of when, not if. The priority shouldn’t just be keeping hackers out, but stopping an attack on one piece of equipment from spreading to others. If a hacker gets into one freezer, they shouldn’t automatically be able to access every freezer in the supermarket. Businesses need to have safeguards in place to limit the damage, keep essential services running and recover quickly.

items.body:
The Laughing Cow is unveiling one of its most significant product launches in recent years with the introduction of The Laughing Cow Creamery, an entirely new three-product range designed to bring a fresh take on everyday indulgence to the dairy aisle.
Launching exclusively in Tesco from late October 2026, the new range comprises Creamery Spread, Creamery Skyr and Creamery Whipped, expanding The Laughing Cow’s portfolio with three distinctive propositions that combine deliciously creamy taste, simple ingredients and versatile usage occasions.
Made with real milk, fresh cream, carefully selected ingredients and no additives, the range delivers on growing shopper interest in products that balance indulgent taste with ingredient simplicity and nutritional benefits. All three products are a source of calcium, while Creamery Skyr offers an additional protein proposition, containing 10.2g of protein per 100g.
The launch comes as shoppers increasingly seek out quality dairy products that deliver on taste, nutrition and versatility. With protein continuing to influence food choices and growing interest in simple, recognisable ingredients, Creamery brings together these evolving shopper priorities in a range that still prioritises taste and enjoyment.
Building on The Laughing Cow’s cheese-making heritage, the launch introduces new textures, formats and usage occasions designed to bring additional choice and excitement to the dairy aisle, from breakfast and lunch to snacking, cooking and entertaining.
Three ways to enjoy effortless creaminess
The Laughing Cow Creamery range comprises:
- The Laughing Cow Creamery Spread (150g, RRP £2.25*): A rich, smooth and spreadable cheese designed for versatility across hot and cold dishes, from toast and crackers to dips, sauces and cooking.
- The Laughing Cow Creamery Skyr (145g, RRP £2.45*): Combining an ultra-smooth texture with the natural protein of Skyr, the new variant contains 10.2g of protein per 100g. Skyr is similar to yoghurt but known for its naturally high protein content and thick, creamy texture. Creamery Skyr is designed to appeal to shoppers looking for protein-rich options that deliver on taste, whether enjoyed at breakfast, as a snack or after exercise.
- The Laughing Cow Creamery Whipped (210g, RRP £3.00*): Made with French milk and cream, the light and airy whipped cheese offers a distinctive texture and fresh taste, suitable for both sweet and savoury occasions.
Polly Rattue, brand lead at The Laughing Cow, says: “At The Laughing Cow, we’ve always believed that great-tasting cheese can bring a little joy to everyday life. Creamery represents one of our most significant launches in recent years, introducing an entirely new range that brings something fresh and distinctive to the dairy aisle.
We know shoppers increasingly want the best of both worlds: delicious, indulgent taste alongside simple ingredients and meaningful product benefits. With Creamery, we’ve brought those qualities together in three distinctive products that deliver effortless creaminess.
From the rich smoothness of Spread and the natural protein of Skyr to the light, cloud-like texture of Whipped, each product offers something different, giving shoppers more ways to enjoy deliciously creamy cheese throughout the day.
“We’re delighted to be launching Creamery exclusively with Tesco and look forward to introducing shoppers to the range.”

Asda is kicking off the festive food season in style with the launch of its Christmas sandwich range for 2026. Live in stores from yesterday, 2nd of November; customers have plenty of time to enjoy a festive lunch-on-the-go in the run-up to Christmas.
With Christmas sandwiches becoming one of the most anticipated supermarket food launches of the year, Asda’s range features 10 festive mains, with four NEW lines for 2026, and four festive snacks, with three NEW lines for 2026 as part of its popular Meal Deal offering.
Customers will find that Asda’s festive meal deal range got an upgrade for 2026, as for the first time ever, the supermarket is going head-to-head with rivals by introducing premium festive main lines under its ‘Exceptional’ range, offering shoppers more indulgent choices for lunch.
Last year, Asda shoppers purchased more than one million festive sandwiches and wraps during the Christmas season, showing the nation’s appetite for seasonal lunchtime treats.
This Christmas, customers can choose from a mix of returning favourites and exciting new products inspired by flavours of traditional festive feasts, Boxing Day ‘leftovers’ and indulgent seasonal party food.
Asda’s new premium Exceptional sandwiches are set to take centre stage with two new lines landing part of Asda’s Exceptional Meal Deal that includes a premium main, snack and drink for £5.50.
The NEW Exceptional Deli Style Turkey, Brie & Stuffing Sandwich is packed with premium festive ingredients including succulent British turkey, creamy French Brie, traditional pork, sage & onion stuffing, and a sweet cranberry & balsamic onion chutney, all layered in thick-cut tiger bloomer bread for a generous bite.
The NEW Exceptional Italian Antipasti & Mozzarella Wrap brings an Italian-inspired twist to the festive lunch category. A deliciously festive wrap filled with Milano salami, prosciutto cotto ham and creamy mozzarella pearls, finished with a rich spiced fig chutney for a sweet and savoury Italian-inspired twist, this premium wrap combines charcuterie-style ingredients for a unique Christmas offering.
NEW in the standard range, and qualifying for the Asda main, snack and drink for £3.74 Meal Deal is the NEW Asda Boxing Day Curry Wrap, inspired by the classic Boxing Day curry, the wrap combines rich butter chicken with tandoori onions, fresh coriander and cooling mint yoghurt mayo, all wrapped in a soft tortilla for a deliciously festive twist.
So that no one is left behind this Christmas, Asda is also launching a vegan offering this year. The NEW Asda All The Trimmings Vegan Wrap comes with sweet maple roasted vegetables are paired with vegan stuffing, sage & onion vegan mayonnaise, crispy onions and cranberry chutney.
Customers need not fear as Asda’s other popular festive sarnies are also back by popular demand, with improved recipes and high-quality ingredients. The range includes Asda’s well-loved Boxing Day Sandwich, the mega Christmas Club Sandwich and the Christmas Lunch Wrap.
For customers who are ‘Christmas maxxing’ this year, there are also festive snacks to choose from when shopping for sides as part of the Meal Deal offering, including the NEW Choc Orange Brownie Bites Grab Bag for a sweet treat or the NEW Pigs in Blankets with Gravy Mayo Dip for a savoury one.
Asda’s festive sandwich range is available now, in stores and online.
Customers can shop premium sandwiches as part of Asda’s premium main, snack and drink Meal Deal for £5.00, or standard sandwiches as part of the main, snack and drink Meal Deal for £3.74 – with no loyalty cards needed to access the savings.

Developed by Very’s lead creative agency The Gate, and produced by […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Very, the online retailer operated by The Very Group, today unveils its Christmas and Black Friday campaign, ‘That’s the Very Thing’, bringing its brand proposition to life through an expanded cast of animated flamingo characters and a pioneering blend of CGI and AI-assisted animation.
Developed by Very’s lead creative agency The Gate, and produced by M3Labs, the campaign introduces a new flamingo family marking the next chapter in the evolution of one of retail’s most distinctive creative assets.
For the past three years, the online retailer has used the power of creative consistency to maximise impact. Collectively, since launching for the first time at Christmas in 2023, the multi-award-winning platform has doubled brand campaign recognition, whilst also showing significant impacts on brand sentiment, brand trust and brand consideration.
Building on this, and Very’s recent brand evolution, the campaign sees the retailer’s iconic pink box and cube logo become a portal into imaginative worlds inspired by the products, possibilities and moments customers value most during the festive season.
The work supports Very’s ambition to showcase itself as a trusted destination that combines great choice, flexible ways to pay and a shopping experience that feels good.
Launching across TV, streaming, out-of-home, radio and digital channels, ‘That’s the Very Thing’ is the first Very campaign to use a hybrid CGI and AI-assisted production process, combining creative craftsmanship with emerging technology to create a richer and more scalable suite of assets.
The hero 30 second film follows a young flamingo as he searches for his own dream gift, and finds himself transported through the Very cube into the dream worlds of his family along the way. Each flamingo has a moment of escapism, drawn from the great selection of dream gifts available from Very. Back in reality, the flamingo family celebrate Christmas together, made easy with Very’s choice of ways to pay, free delivery and returns.
The film was directed by Peter Lee-Scott who worked with M3Labs and The Gate to shape how CGI and AI were each used, keeping creative craft at the heart of every frame.
Very partnered with System1 Group to test the creative, with the new campaign becoming the online retailer’s highest-scoring ad ever. It ranked among the top 1% of retail ads with its target audience, achieving System1’s top Star Rating of 5.9, outperforming industry benchmarks and creating a strong emotional connection that drove brand recognition.
Helen James, chief executive officer, The Gate, said: “Very’s flamingo campaigns have been a firm favourite among customers since launching in 2023, having significant positive impacts on brand sentiment, trust and consideration, so evolving them was never about starting again – it was about giving them new life and a bigger stage. By working with M3Labs and Director, Peter Lee-Scott, we’ve built a world with real craft, charm and ambition and, just like previous years, we’ve used data and insights to inform the creative approach with System 1 supporting pre-testing.”
Sam Wright, chief customer and commercial officer at The Very Group, commented: “Christmas is one of the most important times of the year for the families we serve, and we’re proud to be able to unveil our latest campaign which takes viewers on a journey to find the very thing to help make Christmas extra special.
“From showcasing the great range of gifts available across our online department store, to highlighting our flexible ways to pay, the new campaign spotlights Very as a Christmas shopping destination.”
The Christmas campaign goes live on 1 November across TV, streaming, out-of-home, radio with direct response TV following from 7 November. Black Friday activity then begins on 12 November across the same TV and streaming channels, with direct response TV from 21 November. Radio runs throughout the period, with always-on activity starting on 31 October. Media planning and buying is handled by Zenith.
Alongside the campaign, a partnership with Platform Media takes ‘That’s the Very Thing’ into the real world, pairing celebrity hosts, across various podcasts, for Secret Santa gifting challenges.
‘That’s the Very thing’ will roll out over a full suite of campaign assets across the festive period, covering product range, more time to pay, and Black Friday communications.

items.body:
Key buyers from major retailers including Aldi, Sainsbury’s and ASDA, are set to meet more than 250 Scottish food and drink business leaders in Aberdeen at the Scotland Food & Drink Industry Conference.
Producers from the length and breadth of Scotland have been invited to hear from and to meet major buyers and influential figures from retail, food service and hospitality as well as government, enterprise agencies and growth partners.
Scotland’s food and drink sector is currently valued at a record £19 billion, a total that the Scotland Food & Drink Industry Conference 2027 aims to increase to £30 billion by 2030.
The conference will be held at the P&J Live arena in Aberdeen for the first time on 3 March 2027 and will feature a wide range of expert speakers on key growth topics including practical support on accessing new markets, growing shelf-space for Scottish products, net zero, and succession planning. The speaker line-up combines sector experts from leadership organisations, the heads of some of Scotland’s most successful food and drink businesses, and major retailers.
Attendees will be the first to access new and exclusive trends data to equip them for building market opportunities, as well as the chance to connect and build relationships with key potential buyers.
Research from The Knowledge Bank, Scotland Food & Drink’s insights hub, found that more than half of Scots said that ‘made in Scotland’ provenance was important to them (51%), and the vast majority (87%) want to be able to buy more food and drink produced in Scotland[1].
The Knowledge Bank also found that more than half (56%) of people in the UK outside of Scotland would like to be able to buy more Scottish food and drink products when grocery shopping[2].
So, while there is a desire for more Scottish products in UK baskets, the conference aims to capitalise on demand on grow the availability of Scottish products on shelves across the country. The Scotland Food & Drink Industry Conference 2027 will provide the support, knowledge and insight to help producers reach build their markets and ultimately grow.
Iain Baxter, CEO of Scotland Food & Drink, said: “Our sector has an £11 billion in potential growth between now and 2030. To achieve that we need to match the ambition of our businesses with the practical tools they need to seize on the opportunity.
“The Scotland Food & Drink Industry Conference in March is a unique opportunity for businesses to be part of the conversation around the future of our sector and empower them with insights, connections, practical guidance and inspiration to realise this growth potential.
“Our sector is unique in its collaboration and shared determination to grow and make Scotland the best place in the world to own, operate or work in a food and drink business. Our £19 billion valuation is a positive reflection on the endeavour and entrepreneurial spirit of our business leaders, but as global appetites for the premium products we produce grows, we have to be prepared to take advantage of that demand.”
ONE Seedpod has been confirmed as headline partner for the event.
Alan Thorpe, director of ONE Food & Drink, said: “We are excited about partnering with Scotland Food & Drink to bring this conference to Aberdeen for the first time. ONE SeedPod is Scotland’s innovation hub and located just up from the conference venue, so we’re looking forward to showing a national audience the exciting innovation and development happening here in the north east of Scotland.”
To find out more about the Scotland Food & Drink Industry Conference 2027 and to book your tickets, please visit: https://industryconference.foodanddrink.scot/

This step down was […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following today’s release of Zalando’s figures for the three months ending 30 September 2026; Louise Deglise-Favre, lead apparel analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Zalando’s revenue growth slowed markedly in Q3 FY2026, rising 5.1% to €3.2bn, down from the 20.8% recorded in the prior quarter. This step down was largely expected, as the prior-year comparative now includes ABOUT YOU, which was consolidated from July 2025, meaning the acquisition no longer flatters reported growth. Even so, growing 5.1% across Europe against a backdrop of tough macroeconomic conditions and cautious consumer spending is an impressive result, and suggests Zalando continues to outperform the wider European apparel market. Adjusted EBIT rose 10.6% to €106.5m, with the margin edging up to 3.4% from 3.2% last year, supported by lower fulfilment costs, ABOUT YOU integration synergies and strong B2B growth. Zalando has confirmed its full-year guidance from August, continuing to expect GMV and revenue growth in the lower half of its 12%–17% range and adjusted EBIT of €680m–€720m.
“In its largest segment, B2C, revenue grew 2.8%, while active customers rose 2.9% to a new high of 63.2m. GMV grew across all three consumer apps, with the marketplace growth now clearly outpacing Zalando’s own retail business. The share of sales through partner brands rose 2.9ppts to 33.6% of B2C GMV, as Zalando is steadily switching to a higher-margin, capital-light platform model, building towards its 2028 target of a 40%–50% partner share. Zalando also unveiled Zalando Extended in November 2026, which brings products from other online shops onto the Zalando app, even though Zalando does not sell them itself. From 2027, customers will be able to buy these items without leaving the app, as Zalando’s own AI agent will complete the purchase for them. Westwing’s home and living range is the first to be added. This will allow Zalando to widen its range without holding any extra stock, while also earning advertising revenue from the shops it brings on board.
“Zalando’s B2B segment accelerated further, with revenue up 27.9%, driven by double-digit growth in Zalando Fulfilment Solutions. This service stores, packs and ships goods for the brands selling on Zalando’s marketplace, allowing Zalando to earn fulfilment fees. The fast-growing partner business is therefore feeding directly into B2B. The segment also continued to benefit from the strategic partnership with NEXT and the launch of Marks & Spencer in 22 markets in August, as well as the addition of Lascana, LC Waikiki and Champion as new clients. Zalando’s ecommerce software solution, SCAYLE, also gained new clients such as N Brown in the UK, and Neighborhood Intelligence, whose portfolio includes Bed Bath & Beyond, in the US. With B2B now generating around 40% of group adjusted EBIT from just over a tenth of revenue, the segment is becoming an increasingly important profit engine, helping to cushion the softer consumer environment.”

items.body:
Subway® is accelerating its restaurant expansion across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) with the aim to double its footprint to 10,000 restaurants by 2031. This builds on a year of strong performance with new and existing partners and the launch of Blueprint, a reimagined restaurant and brand experience.
Highlights from the year across EMEA include:
- Positive net restaurant growth as partners continue to invest in the brand.
- Average unit volumes at a record high reflecting strong guest demand.
- Digital sales up over 20% year-to-date as more guests order through Subway’s app, kiosks and delivery platforms.
Subway is growing through new strategic partnerships, including an expanded development agreement with ASDA that will see up to 70 new restaurants open over the next four years in the UK, increasing the number of Subway restaurants in ASDA stores by more than 50%. The agreement comes after a successful year for ASDA that saw it expand its portfolio to over 120 Subway restaurants.
In the last 18 months, Subway has also signed six new Master Franchise agreements in EMEA, spanning 14 countries across Central Europe, Azerbaijan, the Nordics, Iberia and Qatar. Most recently, Subway announced a new agreement with Emerging Bites to open 300 restaurants across Austria, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia and the Czech Republic over the next ten years, as well as opening Subway’s first restaurants in Azerbaijan with N Sky Build.
“We’re building on a strong foundation across EMEA, with significant opportunities to grow in both existing and new markets,” said Tracy Gehlan, president, Subway EMEA. “Our ambition to double our footprint reflects our confidence in the brand, our development partners and the long-term potential across the region. By expanding in the right locations and improving the experience for our guests and franchisees, we can continue bringing Subway to more guests in EMEA.”
As part of its growth strategy, Subway is also focused on strengthening restaurant economics and helping franchisees increase sales and profitability. Central to this is Blueprint, a reimagined restaurant and brand experience. It brings together a fresh look and feel and a new brand position, Get Your Own Way, along with new occasions including breakfast and coffee, Grab & Go and Subway After Dark, an evening experience with a different menu and mood.
From 1 January 2027, new Subway restaurants and remodels in EMEA will be built to the Blueprint design and operating model, making it the standard for Subway’s growth across the region.

items.body:
Primark is putting fashion and value at the heart of Christmas with the launch of its 2026 ‘Style Your Season’ campaign, bringing together the outfits, moments and finishing touches that make the season special.
Launching today in the windows of more than 500 Primark stores worldwide and across digital and social channels, the campaign showcases styles for every part of the festive season, from statement partywear and cosy knitwear to seasonal homeware and thoughtful gifts. This year also marks Primark’s biggest-ever festive pyjama collection, with matching options for the whole family. With fashion starting from just £1.30 for kids and £5 for adults, Primark is making it easier for customers to find something for every occasion this winter.
Fashion for every festive occasion
At the heart of the campaign is Primark’s festive fashion collection, packed with trend-led pieces and versatile wardrobe staples designed to take customers through every event, from office parties and nights out to family gatherings and last-minute plans.
For those who love an excuse to dress up, Coleen Rooney returns with her third By Coleen collection, putting festive glamour centre stage. From rich velvet and satin to sequins and sparkle, the collection brings plenty of statement-making style, while coordinated looks offer an effortlessly polished approach to party dressing. With prices starting from just £6, the collection will land in Primark stores from next week.
For menswear, Irish actor Emmett J. Scanlan makes his debut as the face of Primark Man’s 2026 Christmas campaign, showcasing a collection that blends heritage with a relaxed, contemporary attitude. Textured and slim-fit suits bring a sharper look for dressing up, while checked car coats, borg-lined jackets and padded bombers offer elevated everyday layers. Modern Fair Isle knits and rich textures add a nostalgic festive touch, creating versatile winter looks that feel relaxed and easy to wear, with prices starting from £10.
For the moments in between
Christmas isn’t just about dressing up; it’s also about slow mornings, cosy nights in and spending time with the people (and pets) who make the season special. From warm knitwear and comfortable layers to matching pyjamas, Primark has the in-between moments covered. Family pyjama styles start from £4 for kids and £8 for adults, with options ranging from classic flannel and tartan to stripes and playful character prints featuring The Grinch, Winnie the Pooh, Mickey Mouse and Home Alone. With matching options for dogs too, the whole family can get involved.
For the finishing touches
Style doesn’t stop at the wardrobe. From cosy nights in to hosting family and friends, Primark’s homeware collection brings seasonal touches to every corner of the home. Inspired by the warmth and nostalgia of celebrations past, the collection pairs much-loved traditional motifs with a cosy, playful feel, spanning illustrated bedding, cushions and throws, seasonal candles, statement decorations and elegant tableware. With prices starting from £1, there are plenty of ways to bring a little Christmas magic home.
For those ticking off their Christmas shopping list, the retailer’s gifting range spans beauty, fragrance, accessories and stocking fillers. And for the person who already has everything, Primark gift cards are available in stores across all markets and online at www.primarkgiftcards.com.
Supporting communities
Alongside this year’s campaign, Primark stores will be giving back locally through the Good Neighbour Fund. The programme empowers stores to support charities and organisations that matter to their colleagues and customers. This festive season, many will be making donations to local causes, helping to make a positive difference in their communities.
Matt Houston, chief customer & digital officer at Primark, said: “The festive season looks different for everyone, and ‘Style Your Season’ is all about helping our customers make every moment their own. We’ve brought together great fashion, quality and value across everything from partywear and matching pyjamas to gifting and homeware. Whatever the occasion, we want our customers to be able to find what they’re looking for at a price they’ll love.”
For more information about Primark’s festive offerings, prices and store availability, visit https://www.primark.com/en-gb.

items.title: UK retailers urged to update refrigeration software following Europe cyber attacks
items.summary: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging UK retailers to update and patch their refrigeration software following a wave of cyber attacks targeting supermarket chillers and freezers across Europe. Hackers have been remotely gaining access to internet-connected refrigeration controllers by exploiting unpatched, exposed, login… This story continues at UK retailers urged to update refrigeration software following Europe cyber attacks Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Hackers have been remotely gaining access to internet-connected refrigeration controllers by exploiting unpatched, exposed, login pages on the open internet rather than private, protected networks.
Attackers have forced fridge and freezer units into continuous defrost or high-temperature cycles, in some cases pushing temperatures to around 50°C which has destroyed tons of fresh and frozen food across several European countries including Ireland, Belgium and France.
No widespread disruptions have been officially confirmed in UK stores yet, but some meat processors have reported temperature spikes.
NCSC’s director for national resilience Jonathon Ellison and chief executive Dr Richard Horne have called on retail leaders to immediately audit their operational technology (OT) environments, apply outstanding software patches/firmware updates, and disconnect direct, unprotected internet exposure from cooling systems.
Dai Vaughan, chief technology officer at digital transformation consultancy Public Digital, commented: “Cyberattacks don’t have to bring down computer systems to cause serious damage. As these supermarket attacks show, something as simple as changing the temperature of a freezer can destroy thousands of pounds worth of stock.
“More and more of the equipment we rely on is now connected to the internet, from supermarket fridges to heating systems and factory machinery. That makes it easier to manage, but it also creates new risks if security isn’t properly considered and maintained. The security of these systems has to keep pace with how much we rely on them.
“Businesses may have outsourced the maintenance of their equipment, but they haven’t outsourced responsibility for what happens when it fails. They need to know who can access these systems remotely, how that access is protected and whether an attacker could use it to cause wider disruption.
“Cyberattacks are a question of when, not if. The priority shouldn’t just be keeping hackers out, but stopping an attack on one piece of equipment from spreading to others. If a hacker gets into one freezer, they shouldn’t automatically be able to access every freezer in the supermarket. Businesses need to have safeguards in place to limit the damage, keep essential services running and recover quickly.
“Cybersecurity can no longer be just about protecting computers and data. It’s now about protecting the everyday equipment that keeps businesses’ doors open.”

items.body:
Asda is pleased to announce that David Potts CBE has been appointed group CEO with immediate effect. In turn, Allan Leighton becomes Non-Executive Group Chairman as planned.
Allan Leighton, group chairman said: “I am really excited to have appointed David as Group CEO. Over the last two years, we have stabilised the business and returned it to some growth and begun to establish Asda as ‘more than a supermarket’ through our Formula for Growth strategy. David has an outstanding record in our industry, his experience is exactly what we now require for the next stage of our transformation and beyond and it will be great to work with him.”
David Potts, group chief executive officer said: “Asda has long been a great business, one I’ve admired and traded against over many years. The colleagues are remarkable, some of the most passionate I’ve met.
“The business has made good progress but significant opportunities remain and I’m delighted and very proud to have been asked by Allan to lead the team.
“Providing value to families across the UK has always been in Asda’s DNA and by making improvements to the shopping trip every week, which customers can experience and feel in their pockets, we will revitalise the business and bring benefits for all our stakeholders, including our 116,296 very hard-working colleagues.
“Christmas is upon us and the business has a clear focus on keeping Asda prices locked low at this important time for our customers. I’m excited to get started.”

items.title: Could your existing in-store network become a retail media channel?
items.summary: Retailers looking to grow in-store media do not always need to start from scratch. An existing digital network can provide a strong foundation if it supports the experience, operations, and commercial needs of a media business… Retail media has expanded beyond retailer websites and apps. Stores are increasingly part of the opportunity: a place to...
items.body:
Retailers looking to grow in-store media do not always need to start from scratch. An existing digital network can provide a strong foundation if it supports the experience, operations, and commercial needs of a media business…
Retail media has expanded beyond retailer websites and apps. Stores are increasingly part of the opportunity: a place to reach shoppers close to the point of decision, in a context that online channels cannot fully replicate.
For retailers, the question is how to build that opportunity without creating a second, disconnected operation. Many already have a digital in-store network that supports customer information, promotions, and brand content. Could that network do more?
In many cases, yes. The first step is to understand what it can already do and what would need to change to support paid campaigns.
Start with the network you have
An established network may already reach shoppers across locations and store formats. It may have content workflows, local teams and technology partners in place. Those are valuable foundations.
But a retail media channel has additional requirements. Retailers need to manage advertiser campaigns alongside their own communications, define where and when paid content appears, protect brand standards, and give advertisers clear information about campaign delivery and performance.
That does not mean every retailer needs to replace its existing setup. It means assessing whether the network can support these needs, and how it can connect with the retailer’s wider media, data and operational processes.
Make the experience work for shoppers
Retail media must create value for more than the advertiser. The campaign should fit the shopping environment, make sense in context and sit alongside the information shoppers need.
That calls for thoughtful decisions about placement, timing, relevance and the balance between retailer and brand content. A network that simply adds more advertising may create inventory, but it will not necessarily create a better experience or a stronger proposition for advertisers.
Retailers should ask: what is the shopper doing in this part of the store? What information would help at this moment? How can a brand message add value rather than interrupt? The answers can help shape a media offer that feels native to the store.
Build capability in stages
A retailer does not have to launch every format, measurement option or commercial model at once. A focused starting point can help teams learn what works: select suitable locations, agree campaign rules, establish how content is approved and reported, then expand based on evidence.
Measurement deserves particular attention. Advertisers need confidence that campaigns ran as planned and a clear explanation of what results they can report. Retailers should be precise about what their data can show, how they collect it, and how they will use it. Trust with shoppers and brand partners depends on transparency.
The technology should support this evolution. Retailers need the flexibility to manage paid and owned content together, connect with other systems where needed and adapt the network as commercial requirements develop.
Use the right partners to unlock what is already there
Turning an existing digital network into a media channel involves more than a technical change. It can affect retail media, marketing, store operations, IT, data and external brand partners. Specialist partners can help retailers assess their current estate, plan integrations and deliver a model that works across locations.
Scala is a retail media-ready IXM platform that lets retailers use their existing digital in-store networks and develop them for retail media. Working through specialist partners, Scala helps retailers connect the experience they want to create with the practical requirements of managing it across their estate.
The opportunity is not simply to sell more advertising. It is to build a useful, well-managed in-store media offer from the assets retailers already have. One that gives brands meaningful access to shoppers while keeping the store experience at its centre.

items.title: Asda appoints former Morrisons boss as chief executive as sales struggle
items.summary: David Potts to take over immediately as executive chair Allan Leighton steps back to non-executive strategic role Business live – latest updates Asda has appointed David Potts, the 69-year-old former boss of Morrisons, as its chief executive with immediate effect as it continues to struggle to lift sales. The UK’s third largest supermarket said its 73-year-old executive chair, Allan Leighton, who has been running the business since 2024 , would now step back to a non-executive role focusing on “the long-term strategic agenda for the business”. Continue reading...
items.body:
Asda has appointed David Potts, the 69-year-old former boss of Morrisons, as its chief executive with immediate effect as it continues to struggle to lift sales.
The UK’s third largest supermarket said its 73-year-old executive chair, Allan Leighton, who has been running the business since 2024, would now step back to a non-executive role focusing on “the long-term strategic agenda for the business”.
Potts began his career on the shop floor at Tesco aged 16 and worked at the UK’s biggest supermarket for decades, eventually heading its UK business. He was then chief executive of Morrisons between 2015 and 2023, leaving after the supermarket group was taken private by the US investment house Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2021.
Asda and Morrisons are struggling as they face heavy competition and high levels of debt. Aldi is poised to overtake Asda to become the UK’s third largest supermarket, with about one percentage point separating them. Asda’s sales fell by 0.5% in the three months to 4 October, according to the latest figures from the market research group Worldpanel by Numerator, despite its efforts to trim prices and improve its ranges and availability of stock.
The appointment of Potts comes after a long search for a chief executive by Asda and is a surprise move as Leighton had indicated he expected to fill the role with an internal candidate.
Leighton said he was “really excited” to appoint Potts. “Over the last two years, we have stabilised the business and returned it to some growth and begun to establish Asda as ‘more than a supermarket’ through our Formula for Growth strategy. David has an outstanding record in our industry, his experience is exactly what we now require for the next stage of our transformation and beyond and it will be great to work with him,” Leighton said.
 
Potts said: “Asda has long been a great business, one I’ve admired and traded against over many years. The colleagues are remarkable, some of the most passionate I’ve met. The business has made good progress but significant opportunities remain and I’m delighted and very proud to have been asked by Allan to lead the team.
“Providing value to families across the UK has always been in Asda’s DNA and by making improvements to the shopping trip every week, which customers can experience and feel in their pockets, we will revitalise the business and bring benefits for all our stakeholders, including our 116,296 very hard-working colleagues.”
He added: “Christmas is upon us and the business has a clear focus on keeping Asda prices locked low at this important time for our customers. I’m excited to get started.”

items.summary: Asda has appointed former Morrisons executive David Potts as the next CEO, effective immediately. The current CEO, Allan Leighton, is set to take on the role of non-executive group chairman…
items.body:
Asda appoints former Morrisons executive David Potts as CEO
Asda has appointed former Morrisons executive David Potts as the next CEO, effective immediately.
The current CEO, Allan Leighton, is set to take on the role of non-executive group chairman as previously planned by the supermarket retailer.
As part of his new role as non-executive chairman, Allan Leighton will focus on the long-term strategic plan for the business.
Potts brings years of experience in senior leadership positions across major UK supermarket retailers to the role.
He began his career at Tesco, where he was eventually promoted to the CEO of the Ireland, UK and Asia business before joining Morrisons.
During his tenure as CEO of Morrisons, Potts oversaw a financial turnaround and business restructure before the transition to private ownership.

David Potts, Group CEO said: “Asda has long been a great business, one I’ve admired and traded against over many years.
“The business has made good progress, but significant opportunities remain, and I’m delighted and very proud to have been asked by Allan to lead the team.
“Providing value to families across the UK has always been in Asda’s DNA, and by making improvements to the shopping trip every week, which customers can experience and feel in their pockets, we will revitalise the business and bring benefits for all our stakeholders, including our 116,296 very hard-working colleagues.”
This leadership change comes as the supermarket retailer continues to push towards a financial turnaround, recently reporting improved results in the seven weeks to 18 August.
Asda has returned to like-for-like sales growth for the first time in more than two years, and the new CEO will be responsible for continuing the recovery process at the supermarket retailer.

items.title: Subway targets 10,000 restaurants, supported by Asda partnership
items.summary: Subway has unveiled plans to double its restaurant estate across Europe, the Middle East and Africa to 10,000 sites by 2031, supported by new franchise agreements and an expanded partnership…
items.body:
Subway targets 10,000 restaurants, supported by Asda partnership
Subway has unveiled plans to double its restaurant estate across Europe, the Middle East and Africa to 10,000 sites by 2031, supported by new franchise agreements and an expanded partnership with Asda.
The sandwich chain is accelerating its expansion following a year of growth across the region, with digital sales rising more than 20 per cent year to date and average sales per restaurant reaching record levels.
In the UK, Subway has extended its partnership with Asda, with plans to open up to 70 additional restaurants inside the supermarket chain’s stores over the next four years.
The agreement will increase Subway’s presence across Asda’s estate by more than 50 per cent, building on the more than 120 restaurants already operating within its supermarkets.
Subway has also signed six master franchise agreements across 14 countries in the past 18 months, covering markets including Central Europe, Azerbaijan, the Nordics, Iberia and Qatar.
Its latest agreement with Emerging Bites will see 300 restaurants open across Austria, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia and the Czech Republic over the next decade.
The chain has also entered Azerbaijan through a partnership with N Sky Build.
Subway EMEA president Tracy Gehlan said: “We’re building on a strong foundation across EMEA, with significant opportunities to grow in both existing and new markets.
“Our ambition to double our footprint reflects our confidence in the brand, our development partners and the long-term potential across the region.”
Alongside its expansion plans, Subway is introducing a new restaurant format called Blueprint, which will become standard across new openings and refurbished sites in EMEA from 1 January 2027.
The concept includes a redesigned restaurant interior, alongside additional food and drink occasions such as breakfast and coffee, Grab & Go and Subway After Dark, which will offer a different evening menu and atmosphere.
Blueprint also introduces a new brand positioning, ‘Get Your Own Way’, as Subway looks to attract customers beyond its traditional lunchtime trade.
Gehlan added: “By expanding in the right locations and improving the experience for our guests and franchisees, we can continue bringing Subway to more guests in EMEA.”
The chain said its growth strategy will focus on improving restaurant profitability alongside expanding its estate, with digital ordering through its app, self-service kiosks and delivery platforms continuing to play a larger role in sales.

items.title: Asda hands reins to former Morrisons boss in turnaround push
items.summary: Asda has named a former Morrisons boss as its new chief executive as the embattled grocer looks to accelerate its turnaround efforts. David Potts, who also spent four decades with Tesco, will take over the reins with immediate effect, prompting veteran boss Allan Leighton to step back into a non-executive chairman role two years after [...]
items.body:
Asda hands reins to former Morrisons boss in turnaround push
Asda has named a former Morrisons boss as its new chief executive as the embattled grocer looks to accelerate its turnaround efforts.
David Potts, who also spent four decades with Tesco, will take over the reins with immediate effect, prompting veteran boss Allan Leighton to step back into a non-executive chairman role two years after he returned to the firm.
This comes as Asda sees sales growth for the first time in years, amid huge pressure from discount grocers Aldi and Lidl to keep its prices low and boost the quality of its food offering.
David Potts began his career at Tesco, working his way up from the deli counter to the boss of its Asian operations during a 40-year stint, before becoming chief executive of Morrisons in 2015.
He remained at the helm of Morrisons until it was bought by private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice in 2023, when he was replaced by Rami Baitiéh.
Allan Leighton, who was originally Asda’s chief executive during its 1990s heyday, returned to the supermarket giant as executive chairman in November 2024, tasked with returning the struggling company to its best years.
About-turn for Asda
Potts’s appointment marks a significant shift in direction for the supermarket, which had said it would eventually appoint a chief executive from inside the company’s existing leadership group.
In August, Leighton told City AM that the appointment of a chief executive was “not imminent”. He said: “The preference would be to appoint a CEO from inside the company, and we have a very highly talented group of executives, and my hope is that somebody would emerge from the group.
“But that is not imminent yet because we’re still working with the group that we’ve got to deliver what we’re doing. But that’s the intent.”
Tuesday’s announcement will bring an end to Leighton’s stint as executive chair just two years since his appointment. Leighton said over the summer that his turnaround efforts had brought Asda to the “foothills of recovery”.
He said on Tuesday: “I am really excited to have appointed David as Group CEO. Over the last two years, we have stabilised the business and returned it to some growth and begun to establish Asda as ‘more than a supermarket’ through our Formula for Growth strategy.
“David has an outstanding record in our industry, his experience is exactly what we now require for the next stage of our transformation and beyond and it will be great to work with him.”
Potts said that “significant opportunities” remain in Asda’s turnaround, though he praised the business’s “good progress” under Leighton.
He said: I’m delighted and very proud to have been asked by Allan to lead the team. Providing value to families across the UK has always been in Asda’s DNA and by making improvements to the shopping trip every week, which customers can experience and feel in their pockets, we will revitalise the business and bring benefits for all our stakeholders, including our 116,296 very hard-working colleagues.”
Asda posted 0.2 per cent sales growth over the summer following more than two years of decline. The group fell to a £989m pre-tax loss in 2025, though its net debt fell by £500m to £3.1bn.

items.title: Sports Direct and Nike recruit Erling Haaland for star-studded Christmas advert
items.summary: Sports Direct and Nike have teamed up with Manchester City striker Erling Haaland for a Christmas campaign featuring some of the biggest names in sport and music. The campaign, titled ‘Unwrap Potential‘, also stars Olympic sprinter Dina Asher-Smith, England football captain Leah Williamson, rugby player Henry Pollock and rapper Aitch, who take on the role...
items.body:
Sports Direct and Nike have teamed up with Manchester City striker Erling Haaland for a Christmas campaign featuring some of the biggest names in sport and music.
The campaign, titled ‘Unwrap Potential‘, also stars Olympic sprinter Dina Asher-Smith, England football captain Leah Williamson, rugby player Henry Pollock and rapper Aitch, who take on the role of Christmas gift advisers.
Launching today, the campaign will appear across more than 900 Sports Direct stores internationally, alongside television, social media and digital advertising.
The 60-second advert follows an uncle visiting Sports Direct in search of a Christmas present for his niece, unaware that a team of sporting stars is helping him make the right choice.
Using what the retailer calls ‘Athlete Intelligence’, the team spots the girl’s footballing potential and recommends a pair of Haaland’s Nike Phantom 6 Low football boots.
Aitch also turns to the sporting experts for help finding presents for his sisters.
Created by Chaos x Magic and directed by Tyrus Hill through Park Pictures, the film is supported by five shorter adverts featuring different gifting scenarios, from running and football to trainers and streetwear.
The campaign also includes a series of gift guides curated by the celebrities, offering shoppers recommendations based on their sporting interests and personal style.
Frasers Group chief executive Michael Murray said: “Christmas is our biggest trading moment of the year, and our first-ever brand exclusive Christmas ad with Nike is a powerful example of the Elevation Strategy in action.
“Featuring world-class athletes like Erling Haaland, Unwrap Potential brings the strength of that partnership to life in what promises to be our most impactful Christmas campaign yet.”
Nike EMEA vice president and general manager César García added: “Sport has the power to change how we see ourselves and what we believe is possible.
“Our partnership with Sports Direct is built on a shared ambition to bring more people to sport.”
The campaign will also be promoted across Sports Direct’s UK stores through Frasers Group’s ELEVATE retail media network, which reaches more than 32 million customers through digital screens, connected television and outdoor advertising.

items.title: Supermarket freezers hacked across Europe as cyberattacks destroy food stock
items.summary: Supermarkets across Europe have been forced to throw away thousands of pounds worth of food after hackers took control of their refrigeration systems, sending temperatures soaring to as high as…
items.body:
Supermarket freezers hacked across Europe as cyberattacks destroy food stock
Supermarkets across Europe have been forced to throw away thousands of pounds worth of food after hackers took control of their refrigeration systems, sending temperatures soaring to as high as 50C.
More than 100 stores across at least seven countries were affected by the suspected cyberattacks on Monday, including branches of Carrefour, SuperValu, ICA, Coop, Delhaizeand Ikea.
The disruption saw hackers remotely interfere with refrigeration controls, in some cases activating defrost settings and leaving chilled and frozen products unsellable.
In Sweden, staff at an ICA supermarket in Stockholm discovered their freezers had reached 50C after an attack reportedly took place at around 2am.
“Everything is destroyed,” sales manager Engla Ingwall told Reuters.
Irish supermarket chain SuperValu confirmed that 13 of its 223 stores had been affected by an incident involving a specific model of refrigeration system, with chilled and frozen products removed from sale.
In Belgium, Carrefour reported problems at 15 of its 700 stores, while Ahold Delhaize said dozens of its supermarkets across Belgium and Luxembourg had been affected by an IT incident.
Five Spar stores operated by Colruyt Group also reported refrigeration failures, alongside several Intermarché locations.
Ikea confirmed that its store in Mons, Belgium, had been affected, forcing it to remove some food products as a precaution.
The financial consequences have been immediate for some businesses. Luc De Laet, owner of Belgian butchery chain De Laet & Van Haver, told Sky News he had lost around £12,500 worth of meat after the temperature in his store’s refrigerators rose to 18C.
The incidents follow a similar attack in France last month, when hackers interfered with refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets, including stores operated by Intermarché, Carrefour, Leclerc and Monoprix.
The French attack affected as many as 700 stores, leaving retailers with substantial food losses and prompting a criminal investigation.
Cybersecurity concerns grow
The latest incidents have raised questions about the security of internet-connected refrigeration equipment, which allows retailers to monitor and adjust temperatures remotely.
Danish engineering firm Danfoss, whose refrigeration controllers were among those targeted in France, has previously advised customers to install security updates and strengthen network protections.
Stephan Moelans, chief executive of Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel, confirmed that the latest disruption involved hackers remotely switching refrigeration units into defrost mode.
The company mobilised technicians overnight to disconnect affected systems and prevent further damage.
Cybersecurity experts have warned that older refrigeration controllers connected directly to the internet can leave retailers vulnerable to attacks capable of destroying perishable stock within hours.
The European Union’s food and agriculture commissioner, Christophe Hansen, condemned the incidents as a deliberate attempt to interfere with Europe’s food supply chain and damage consumer confidence.
Belgium’s prosecutor’s office has opened a criminal investigation, while Sweden’s national cybersecurity centre is responding to incidents affecting retailers across the country.
No group has claimed responsibility, and authorities have not established whether the latest attacks and those in France were carried out by the same perpetrators.

items.title: Black Friday discount war risks backfiring as UK shoppers cut budgets by a third
items.summary: More consumers are expected to shop the Black Friday sales in 2026, but a sharp fall in planned spending is forcing retailers to rethink blanket promotions, high-value baskets and the true cost of chasing volume. UK spending across Black Friday and Cyber Monday is forecast to fall 32 per cent to £9.9bn this year, according...
items.body:
More consumers are expected to shop the Black Friday sales in 2026, but a sharp fall in planned spending is forcing retailers to rethink blanket promotions, high-value baskets and the true cost of chasing volume.
UK spending across Black Friday and Cyber Monday is forecast to fall 32 per cent to £9.9bn this year, according to research from ecommerce marketing platform Omnisend. The comparable estimate for 2025 was £14.5bn, while average expected spend per shopper has dropped 31.5 per cent, from £390 to £267.
That contraction comes despite broader participation. The proportion of consumers who say they will buy nothing has fallen from 29.8 per cent to 24.8 per cent, suggesting retailers could see plenty of traffic without the same level of revenue. For merchants already balancing higher costs with cautious demand, the gap between shopper numbers and shopper value makes margin discipline increasingly important.
Marty Bauer, ecommerce expert at Omnisend, warns: “Retailers are facing a different Black Friday maths problem this year. They may have more shoppers willing to take part, but those customers are bringing less money to the sale.”
High spenders retreat as lower budgets grow
The most pronounced shift is at the top end of the market. Just 5.1 per cent of UK respondents intend to spend at least £1,000 during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, down from 12.7 per cent in 2025. The share planning to spend between £500 and £999 has also declined, from 14.3 per cent to 9.6 per cent.
At the other end of the scale, the proportion expecting to spend less than £100 has more than doubled, rising from 8.7 per cent to 18.4 per cent. The £100 to £249 bracket has grown from 20.8 per cent to 24.2 per cent. Although these are stated intentions rather than completed transactions, the figures point to smaller baskets and more selective purchasing at a moment when retailers traditionally compete aggressively on price.
Clothing and accessories lead planned purchases, cited by 39 per cent of respondents, followed by technology and electronics at 36.5 per cent, toys and games at 31.2 per cent, and beauty or self-care at 24.2 per cent. Food and drink is on the list for 18.2 per cent, potentially creating opportunities for grocery, gifting and specialist food businesses that can present a clear value proposition without relying on deep, store-wide reductions.
Bauer cautioned against interpreting constrained budgets as a reason to cut prices across every category. “The worst response to a smaller spending budget is a bigger blanket discount. For a business with narrow margins, cutting prices across the whole range can create plenty of activity without leaving much profit to show for it.”
Selective offers could beat site-wide discounts
The challenge is particularly acute for independent retailers, which may lack the scale or supplier leverage of the largest marketplaces. Bauer argued that smaller operators should avoid trying to compete line by line with Amazon and instead use customer data to decide which products, audiences and incentives merit investment.
“Independent retailers don’t need to match Amazon on every price,” he notes. “They need to be more selective about the products they promote and the customers they are trying to reach. Someone who has bought from you before or shown an interest in a particular product is a far better starting point than sending the same offer to everyone.”
That could mean shifting the emphasis from headline percentage cuts to offers designed around customer behaviour. Bundles can increase perceived value, loyalty promotions can reward known shoppers, and a carefully set free-delivery threshold can encourage a bigger basket. However, each mechanic needs to be assessed against fulfilment, acquisition and product costs rather than judged on sales volume alone.
As Bauer puts it: “A carefully chosen bundle, a limited offer for loyal customers or a realistic free-delivery threshold may offer better value than a site-wide discount. But retailers need to work out what each incentive costs them before it goes live. A larger order isn’t necessarily better if the margin has disappeared.”
Earlier shopping raises the stakes
Separate Omnisend holiday shopping research found that 84 per cent of UK respondents expect rising prices to affect their purchasing decisions. Price and affordability was the most frequently cited consideration when buying, at 63.5 per cent, while 28.3 per cent said they were beginning festive shopping earlier than usual.
That earlier start could weaken the value of waiting until the traditional Black Friday weekend to launch a campaign. “Timing matters too,” Bauer says. “Some households are shopping earlier to spread the expense, so waiting until Black Friday itself could mean missing customers whose budgets have already been spent elsewhere. Relevant email and SMS offers can help retailers reach those people without paying to compete for every click.”
Consumers are also widening the tools they use to find and fund purchases. Some 12.5 per cent plan to use Buy Now, Pay Later, with a further 27.4 per cent open to doing so for a big-ticket deal. Meanwhile, 17.5 per cent said they had used generative AI to find online deals or coupons during the previous six months, underlining how easily shoppers can compare offers and search for additional savings.
Black Friday remains the most anticipated festive sales event in the research, with 54.5 per cent planning to shop online and 32.1 per cent in store. Cyber Monday, which falls on 30 November, is expected to attract 20 per cent.
The opportunity for retailers is therefore still substantial—but success may depend less on recording a surge in orders than on ensuring each transaction makes commercial sense.
Bauer concludes: “Black Friday will still bring shoppers through the door and onto retail websites. The challenge is making those purchases worthwhile for both sides, rather than chasing sales figures that look impressive but don’t add up.”

items.title: Hugo Boss outlook worsens after Mike Ashley’s Frasers takes control
items.summary: Hugo Boss has cut its outlook for sales and profit in the face of weakening consumer demand, just days after Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group took control of the German fashion house. The luxury retailer had been expecting its performance to take a hit from its turnaround plan but told shareholders this has been worsened by [...]
items.body:
Hugo Boss outlook worsens after Mike Ashley’s Frasers takes control
Hugo Boss has cut its outlook for sales and profit in the face of weakening consumer demand, just days after Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group took control of the German fashion house.
The luxury retailer had been expecting its performance to take a hit from its turnaround plan but told shareholders this has been worsened by a “persistently subdued consumer environment”.
Analysts described this update as a blow to Frasers, the FTSE 250-listed retail group which gained control of Hugo Boss last week following a months-long pursuit.
The German fashion house told shareholders it expects to post full-year earnings of between €250m and €300m, below previous expectations of between €300m and €350m.
Hugo Boss said its full-year sales will decline by a high-single digit percentage, while it had previously been expecting takings to slip by a mid- to high-single figure.
The group blamed this on “softer demand” and the impact of its investment in new technology, including artificial intelligence.
The German fashion house’s sales declined by five per cent in the third quarter, marking a slight improvement on the year-to-date drop of seven per cent. It blamed “macroeconomic headwinds” for this performance.
Chief executive Daniel Grieder said: “Our top-line performance reflected both the deliberate strategic realignment of our business and a persistently subdued consumer environment. At the same time, we made further progress in improving our gross margin and operating efficiencies.
“With demand likely to remain volatile in the fourth quarter, we are adjusting our full-year 2026 outlook to reflect a more realistic assessment of the market environment. Our strategic direction, however, remains unchanged.”
‘Negative’ result for Frasers
Last week, Frasers pushed its stake in Hugo Boss above 50 per cent, making it a subsidiary of the group, which also owns Flannels, Harvey Nichols and Sports Direct.
This marked the end of Frasers’s long struggle to gain control of the German fashion house, as it aims to push into the luxury retail market. The firm has also pushed up its stake in British fashion house Burberry in recent weeks.
Michael Murray, chief executive of Frasers and Ashley’s son-in-law, was appointed chair of Hugo Boss’s supervisory board in September after its existing boss departed due to “recent changes in the company’s shareholder structure”.
Analysts at stock broker RBC said Hugo Boss’s worsening outlook is a “negative read for Frasers Group”.
They said they expect “renewed momentum” from the fashion house next year but added that “visibility on this is low, especially given ongoing political uncertainty”.
Frasers has been criticised in the past for making hostile moves to take control of rival companies, but Grieder told analysts on Tuesday that Hugo Boss “values them as a significant long term shareholder”.
He said: “It’s not a short-term investment for them. They really want to grow the brand with us, and they see big opportunities in the brand. […] So far we really enjoy working and having this dialogue together, and especially with Michael [Murray] as the new chairman.”

items.title: John Lewis Christmas ad stars Kristin Scott Thomas as glamorous granny on a gift hunt
items.summary: Company tugs at heartstrings with Pickles the talking toy dog as it celebrates 20 years of blockbuster festive ads Review: Kristin Scott Thomas v Pickles the evil AI overlord puppy John Lewis has turned to a celebrity best known for playing aristocrats to put a playful but rather upmarket spin on the countdown to Christmas with this year’s festive ad, which features a toy dog called Pickles and a glamorous granny. Kristin Scott Thomas, known for playing upper-crust characters in films such as Four Weddings and a Funeral and the Apple TV show Slow Horses, is cast as Gloria, a grandmother searching for gift inspiration, with the tagline “don’t give up on giving”. Continue reading...
items.body:
John Lewis has turned to a celebrity best known for playing aristocrats to put a playful but rather upmarket spin on the countdown to Christmas with this year’s festive ad, which features a toy dog called Pickles and a glamorous granny.
Kristin Scott Thomas, known for playing upper-crust characters in films such as Four Weddings and a Funeral and the Apple TV show Slow Horses, is cast as Gloria, a grandmother searching for gift inspiration, with the tagline “don’t give up on giving”.
In the 20th version of its blockbuster Christmas ad, the department store kickstarts the official countdown to Christmas by tugging at the heartstrings, with Pickles, voiced by the comedian Paul Whitehouse, challenging Gloria to “do better than cash” when choosing a gift for her grandchildren.
Pickles drags Gloria out of the house on a last-minute mission to find gifts, and after rejecting options in other shops, she sets off on a magical tuk-tuk ride to John Lewis, where she snaps up some disco balls and fairy lights to create a “gran cave” to hang out with her grandchildren, Freddie and Maggie.
Rosie Hanley, the marketing director of John Lewis, said the retailer had increased its spend on this year’s festive ad as the cost of production had risen and it wanted to “push the boat out” for its 20th year.
However, she said the company was confident it would see “a really strong return on our investment” as it tries to grab shoppers’ attention before the Black Friday discount period later this month.
She said the company had wanted the ad “to be more joyful” this year because “things are tough for lots of families”. Despite concerns among British households about higher energy bills and housing costs, Hanley said spending on Christmas-related gear at John Lewis was already up on last year.
The ad, set to a Sam Fender version of the Rolling Stones song You Can’t Always Get What You Want, features a range of John Lewis products in different price brackets, including the £12.99 Fisher-Price pull-along toy dog and a £255 Weekend Max Mara top and matching £290 skirt worn by Gloria.
The three-minute ad will launch on social media on Tuesday morning, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, before a 60-second version airs for the first time on TV in the ad breaks for ITV’s Coronation Street and Channel 4’s The Great British Bake Off on Tuesday evening.
John Lewis will also erect a giant Christmas tree outside its store on London’s Oxford Street to mark the recent pedestrianisation of the road. The company said the numbers of visitors to its store on the street last week were up by more than a fifth on the same week last year.
This year’s ad, created by the Saatchi & Saatchi agency, returns to a formula of using a cute character – such as Monty the penguin in 2014 and Buster the boxer in 2016 – after two years foregrounding other family relationships. However, it has the twist of focusing on the relationship between Pickles and a grandmother rather than centring on cute children.
Hanley said the ad was inspired by research which had revealed that 52% of grandparents give cash as presents because they are not sure what youngsters really want. “People want to give thoughtful gifts but can often lack confidence, so resort to giving cash,” she said.
Now considered a national moment which invites social media comment and skits, the first big-budget John Lewis festive TV ad launched in 2007, soundtracked by a piece of music by Prokofiev.
Previous John Lewis Christmas TV ads have been soundtracked by covers including the Smiths song Please, Please, Please, Let Me Get What I Want and Together in Electric Dreams by Giorgio Moroder and Philip Oakey. Last year’s ad included the 1990s club classic Where Love Lives by Alison Limerick.
This year’s track, which features the choir from the John Spence community high school, which Fender previously attended, and the Easington Colliery Band, will be released on vinyl later this month, with proceeds going to Action For Children. Pickles the dog is based on an existing Fisher-Price pull-along toy called Little Snoopy that is celebrating its 60th year.
The John Lewis ad launch comes hot on the heels of other festive ads for most of the big supermarkets that kicked off last weekend. Total ad spending across the festive period is set to reach £14bn, up 8.2% year-on-year according to the annual review by the Advertising Association and research group WARC. That growth is led by an 18.5% year-on-year surge in social media spend, while total TV spending is expected to be up by 1.6%.
